decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 6 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee voted today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 6 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target of 6 percent to slow down demand.

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 25 basis point increase in the discount rate to 5-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Board of Governors raised the discount rate, which is the rate charged when banks borrow short-term credit directly from the Fed, by 25 basis points to 5-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Economic conditions and considerations addressed by the Committee are essentially the same as when the Committee met in February.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that overall economic conditions remained largely unchanged since their prior meeting.

changes.quote: The Committee remains concerned that increases in demand will continue to exceed the growth in potential supply, which could foster inflationary imbalances that would undermine the economy's record economic expansion.
changes.explanation: Policymakers worried that strong consumer and business demand was outpacing the economy's ability to supply goods and services, threatening inflation.

changes.quote: Against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the Committee believes the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate heightened inflation pressures in the foreseeable future.
changes.explanation: The Fed viewed the future economic risks as tilted toward higher inflation.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.12% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate; the 10-year was 6.13% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 8.23% would fall by about $10.53 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 218k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.2% over the past year (February 2000); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that future policy moves will depend on whether demand continues to outpace supply and drive up inflation pressures. This educational forecast reflects the data available at the time of the meeting.
